proved_2026-08-09: The runtime lives exactly once. guard.py: claim_singleton(home) — fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on <instance>/run.lock, ONE syscall deciding what no read can (read-then-act reopens the race the carries clause named), held for the winner's whole life with no unlock path (the runner's release is its death, by design). flock over the ticket's own 'O_EXCL' suggestion, measured not argued: the SIGKILL tooth shows the kernel releasing a corpse's claim instantly — bare O_EXCL would have left a stale claim needing a second staleness protocol, reopening the race at break-the-claim. The lock file is separate from liveness.json because os.replace churns the record's inode every beat (the churn tooth pins this: 50 replaces, claim unshaken). The door guards ITSELF: main() claims before constructing, so superclaude — or anything — gains a CALL, not a policy (Law 1/6); a loser reads the RECORD, names pid+age (or the dead-but-held lack — the lock outranks a stale read, so alive-but-slow is never doubled), exits 3 (distinct from crash's 1 and argparse's 2). Live fire: two simultaneous launches -> exactly one resident loop, the loser hitting the dead-but-held branch in the wild, a third launch refusing against LIVE, SIGTERM -> clean 0 -> DEAD 7s later. 17/17 teeth green twice + netns seal; verdict verdict-20260809T114947-0fc75d96e523 (all 5 criteria pass, all 4 hypotheses confirmed). Ladder rung 1 closes its remaining red: the loop now starts exactly once — what KEEPS it running across sessions stays the host-seam unit-file IOU.

intent: superclaude — and any other entry point — starts the ground loop if and only if one is not already running, deciding by READING the liveness record, never by scanning for a process.
why: Akien named superclaude as ONE OF the entry points, so the guard cannot live in superclaude: it is a shared door and belongs with the thing it protects (Law 6). Otherwise every future entry point re-derives it, which is Law 1's defect.
falsifier: Two entry points launched simultaneously produce TWO loops — the expensive direction, and the one the atomic claim exists for. Or: a loop alive but merely slow is declared dead inside the 5s window and a second is started beside it. Or: the guard reads liveness by scanning for a process instead of reading the record, which would work and would still be wrong — the record is the owned answer (Law 6).
carries: the ATOMIC claim. The staleness threshold is no longer an open question — 5 seconds, ruled 2026-07-31, recorded in the_threshold. What is still this ticket's to get right is that read-then-act is not atomic: two entry points can both read DEAD inside the same 5s window and both start a loop. The claim must be atomic (O_EXCL create or equivalent), and it is the expensive direction — a missed start is visible, a double start fires every callback twice.

Adding a ground-loop start to it NOW would widen a ticket while it is being proved — the quiet scope creep that makes a proof mean less than it says. Proposed: let it reach PROVED on its ruled scope, and land the call as this ticket's own work against the launcher afterward. Akien's call to overrule.

A cursor AT a stage means that stage was ENTERED — superclaude-starts-itself rests at [PROVEME] with its BUILDME gate already satisfied — so [BUILDME] on a freshly cast leaf claims a crossing that never rode the chokepoint. It cannot have: since ticket buildme-rides-the-chart (2026-07-29) the entry gate refuses a BUILDME crossing unless a berthed validate packet claims the ticket, and a census of all 89 berths finds ZERO claiming any ticket in this family. Hand-writing the cursor forward is precisely the hand-edit of a record of truth that transitions.emit exists to prevent (Law 4). The stage is reachable only by /chart, then the door.
the_threshold: THE STALENESS THRESHOLD IS 5 SECONDS — five missed ticks at the ruled once-per-second cadence. Ruled by Akien 2026-07-31. Three times the interval is the standard liveness heuristic; five gives slack for a loaded box without anyone noticing the lag. LIVE = last-run within 5s. DEAD = last-run older than 5s, whatever the file says about state, whatever pid it names. A crashed loop leaves the file behind but STOPS ADVANCING THE TIMESTAMP — that is the whole detector, and it is Akien's, present in the design from the first telling.
